title: Field Guide plugin: its own guide
about: The Field Guide plugin for Claude Code, mapped with itself: a bundled CLI that projects vendor, the two skills that build and update a guide, and the tests that prove the check.
overview: Projects run one bundled file, dist/guide.mjs, built from src/. Its lookup prints one system's entry, its check keeps every file on the map and every name real, and its render command writes a page. The plugin's two skills drive Claude through a build (inventory, confirmed grouping, parallel drafting, adversarial fact-check) and an update (re-check the systems whose files changed). The test suite proves every check assertion by injecting the defect it exists for.

systems.name: Lookup
systems.oneLiner: Prints one system, a file's owner, or the systems that mention a word.
systems.summary: The pure functions behind `guide <id | path | word>`: glob matching, path normalisation, ownership, the plain-text entry and index, and word search. They read no files, so the check and the lookup share them and cannot disagree about who owns a file.
journey: A session runs node docs/field-guide/guide.mjs with an id, a path or words
An exact id prints that system's entry under fixed section labels
A path is normalised (backslashes, a leading ./) and matched against every system's owns globs
Anything else is searched: every word must appear, first in the name and summary, then deeper in the entry

keyFiles.what: Glob matching, ownersOf, renderSystem, renderIndex and search.
The guide.json and guide.config.json shapes, job kinds and reserved command words.

connects.why: The command line prints through these functions.
The check asserts against the same ownership and rendering code.

watchOuts: Never let the check import the renderer's section labels, because a check that reads its subject's own list stays green when that list is reordered.
Always keep `[` and `(` literal in globs, because Next.js and SvelteKit folder names use them.

systems.name: Command line
systems.oneLiner: Parses the arguments, finds the guide folder and runs the right command.
systems.summary: The entry point of dist/guide.mjs. It finds the folder holding guide.config.json (the --dir flag, then the script's own folder, then ./docs/field-guide), resolves the repo root, lists the repo's files with git, and dispatches to a subcommand or the lookup.
journey: The vendored script starts and parses flags
It locates guide.config.json and the repo root
A subcommand runs, or the lookup prints an entry
A usage error exits 2; a failed check or an unmatched lookup exits 1

keyFiles.what: Argument parsing, the help text and the command dispatch.
Finding the guide folder and repo root, loading config, listing files with git ls-files.

switches.name: --dir
switches.what: Points the CLI at a non-default guide folder.

switches.name: --search
switches.what: Searches every word, even when the first one is a command name.

connects.why: Prints entries, owners and search hits.
Runs `guide check` and sets the exit code.
Runs init, inventory, merge, changed and stamp.

watchOuts: Never add a subcommand without adding it to SUBCOMMANDS, because a system with that id could then never be printed.
Always list files through git ls-files with --others, because a new untracked file must fail the check before it is committed.
Never let a command accept stray words, because `guide stamp duty` would move the update baseline instead of searching.

systems.name: The check
systems.oneLiner: Fails when a file is off the map or a name the guide uses is gone.
systems.summary: `guide check` runs 39 named assertions in five sections: shape, coverage, names, the optional stack add-ons, and the lookup. It reads files and runs git only. It proves the map and the names, never the prose.
journey: It loads the config and guide.json and lists the repo's files
Shape: every system has every field, a known group and real prose
Coverage: every file in scope is owned and every glob matches
Names: key files, rules, checks, jobs, switches, models, connections and flows all exist
Add-ons claim every data model, package script, workflow, cron and rule file
Lookup: each printed entry carries every field under its own label and stays under the size ratchet

keyFiles.what: Every assertion, its stable code (CHECK_CODES) and the text report.

switches.name: entryMaxChars
switches.what: The ratchet on one printed entry's length.

switches.name: --json
switches.what: Prints the results and every assertion code as JSON.

connects.why: Asserts against the same ownership and rendering functions sessions use.
The suite injects a defect for every assertion code.

watchOuts: Never add an assertion without a defect in test/run.mjs that turns its code red, because the suite fails on any unproven code.
Always skip the guide folder and rendered pages when searching for switches, because they name every switch and would make the search vacuous.

systems.name: Rendered page
systems.oneLiner: Writes the guide as one self-contained, offline HTML page.
systems.summary: `guide render` injects the guide JSON, plus counts taken from the repo, into a neutral page template at a marker. The page uses system fonts and inline script only, so it makes no network request, and it escapes `<` so data cannot close the script element.
journey: The command counts files, jobs, models and checks and reads the commit
It replaces the template's marker with the JSON
A reader picks a system tile and its dossier opens beside the map

keyFiles.what: Collects the stats and injects the JSON at the marker.
The page: groups of tiles, the dossier, jobs table, glossary, light and dark themes.

connects.why: Runs when a user types guide render.
The bundler inlines the template as a string.

watchOuts: Never load fonts or scripts from a CDN in the template, because the page must work offline and publish anywhere.
Always keep the template's glob function identical to the CLI's, because the page's path search must agree with the lookup.

systems.name: Build and update helpers
systems.oneLiner: Vendors the CLI, inventories the repo, merges agent output and tracks changes.
systems.summary: The commands the skills drive. init copies the CLI into the project and detects a config; inventory lists the files by folder; merge folds drafting and fact-check JSON (a file, or a run folder read in name order) into guide.json, counts changed fields and can remove glossary terms and flows; changed maps files changed since a commit to their systems (paths read with -z, relative to the root, so non-ASCII names and monorepo packages work); stamp records the verified commit.
journey: init vendors the CLI and writes the config, README and .gitignore
inventory shows folder sizes and the instruction files to name in prompts
merge applies each agent's JSON and reports changed fields, findings and notes
changed and stamp drive the update skill from one verified commit to the next

keyFiles.what: init (vendoring, add-on detection) and inventory.
merge, changed and stamp.
The README init writes into a project's guide folder.

switches.name: --dry-run
switches.what: Reports what merge would change without writing.

switches.name: --unowned
switches.what: Makes inventory list only the files no system owns.

connects.why: The build and update skills run these commands.
changed and inventory use the same ownership matching.

watchOuts: Always write guide.json back with its own line endings, because a CRLF checkout would otherwise show every line changed.

systems.name: Build and update skills
systems.oneLiner: The procedures Claude follows to build a guide and keep it current.
systems.summary: Two user-invoked skills. /field-guide:build inventories the repo, proposes systems for the user to confirm, fans out drafting subagents, then adversarial fact-checkers, and wires in the check and a session pointer. /field-guide:update re-checks only the systems whose files changed.
journey: The user runs /field-guide:build
Claude vendors the CLI, inventories the repo and proposes systems
The user confirms the grouping
Drafting subagents write entries in parallel; fact-check subagents correct them
The check goes green, the page renders, and the user picks how sessions and CI find the guide

keyFiles.what: The build procedure, step by step, and the cost table.
The update procedure.
The prompt each drafting subagent receives.
The prompt each adversarial fact-checker receives.
The field rules pasted into both prompts.
Templates for the CLAUDE.md block, project skill and CI workflow.

switches.name: disable-model-invocation
switches.what: Keeps Claude from starting a costly build or update unasked.

connects.why: Every step runs a CLI command.
The plugin manifest makes the skills installable.

watchOuts: Always name the project's instruction files in each subagent prompt, because subagents do not load path-scoped rules on their own.
Never let a fact-checker check a batch it drafted, because it would defend its own errors.

systems.name: Plugin manifests and docs
systems.oneLiner: Makes the repo installable as a Claude Code plugin and explains it.
systems.summary: The repository is both the plugin and its own marketplace: plugin.json names the plugin, and marketplace.json lists it with source ./ so users add the repo and install from it. The README and license ship with it.
journey: A user adds the repo as a marketplace
They install field-guide from it
Its skills appear as /field-guide:build and /field-guide:update

keyFiles.what: The plugin's name, version and description.
Lists the plugin from this same repo.
What it is, install, cost, limits.

watchOuts: Always bump the version in plugin.json and marketplace.json together, because a set version pins users until it changes.

systems.name: Bundling and tests
systems.oneLiner: Bundles src/ into one file and proves every check assertion.
systems.summary: esbuild bundles src/ and the inlined templates into dist/guide.mjs, which is committed because projects vendor it. The test suite builds a fixture repo in a temp folder, proves every check code red with an injected defect, and exercises every command.
journey: A contributor edits src/ or templates/
npm run build rewrites dist/guide.mjs
npm run check typechecks, fails on a stale dist, and runs the suite and this guide's own check

keyFiles.what: Bundles dist/guide.mjs; --verify fails when it is stale.
Defect injection for every check code, then every command.
The fake repo that exercises every add-on and job kind.
The bundled CLI that projects vendor.

connects.why: Proves each assertion with an injected defect.
Inlines the page template into the bundle.

watchOuts: Always anchor a CLI mutation on text that occurs exactly once in the bundle, because a duplicate anchor mutates the wrong site and proves nothing.
Never edit dist/guide.mjs by hand, because the freshness check rebuilds it from src/.

systems.name: Bundled example
systems.oneLiner: A complete guide the plugin built for ParaFlow, with its rendered page.
systems.summary: examples/paraflow holds the field guide /field-guide:build produced for ParaFlow, an open-source Tauri dictation app, at its commit ecfdf66: the guide, its config and the rendered page. It shows what a finished build looks like before anyone runs one. It is data, not code: the plugin's own check treats it as prose.
journey: A visitor opens examples/paraflow/README.md
They download guide.html and browse the 13 systems
They see the guide.json shape a build writes into docs/field-guide/

keyFiles.what: What the example is, how it was made, and commands to try.
The guide itself: 13 systems, 3 flows, 45 glossary terms.
The rendered page, self-contained and offline.

connects.why: Its guide.html is the template rendered with ParaFlow's guide.

watchOuts: Always regenerate the example from a real build at a stated ParaFlow commit, because hand edits would show readers a guide no build produced.

steps.text: init vendors the CLI; inventory sizes the repo.
Drafting and fact-check subagents write and correct the entries.

The page is written for people to browse.
The session runs the vendored CLI with a path.
It prints the owning system's entry, about 1-3k tokens.

glossary.meaning: Copying the CLI into a project so it runs with plain node, without the plugin.
Breaking the thing a check guards, on purpose, to prove the check goes red.
A limit that may only tighten: trim the content, never raise the number to fit.
